nahhas-irab:1-1.t: وَالنَّازِعاتِ is genitive by the wāw of oath; it was also said that the implied form is "by the Lord of النازعات". Shuʿba related from Sulaymān, from Abū al-Ḍuḥā, from Masrūq, from ʿAbd Allāh, concerning «النازعات»: he said: the angels. And Shuʿba related from al-Suddī, from Abū Ṣāliḥ, from Ibn ʿAbbās, concerning وَالنَّازِعاتِ: he said: [the angel] draws out his soul. So the implied form becomes "by the angels who draw out". غَرْقاً is a maṣdar (verbal noun). Saʿīd ibn Jubayr said: their souls are drawn out, then drowned, then burnt, then cast into the Fire. The implied form is "by the Lord of النازعات", and the meaning is: the souls are drowned, drowning thoroughly (فتغرق غرقا), [as in] وَاللَّهُ أَنْبَتَكُمْ مِنَ الْأَرْضِ نَباتاً [Nūḥ: 17]. [Translator's note: i.e. the maṣdar follows a verb implied by the context, as نباتا follows أنبت rather than its own verb.]

nahhas-irab:10-10.t: يَقُولُونَ, i.e. in this world. أَإِنَّا لَمَرْدُودُونَ فِي الْحافِرَةِ: Ibn Abī Ṭalḥa related from Ibn ʿAbbās concerning فِي الْحافِرَةِ: he said: He is saying "into life". Ibn Zayd said: into the Fire. Mujāhid said: into the earth. On Mujāhid's view the implied form is "into the dug earth (المحفورة)", i.e. into the grave, like مِنْ ماءٍ دافِقٍ [al-Ṭāriq: 6], i.e. poured out (مدفوق); its true sense in Arabic is "of water possessing gushing". On the view of Ibn ʿAbbās, فِي الْحافِرَةِ [means]: we will live as we lived the first time.

nahhas-irab:11-11.t: [The reading «ناخرة»] is soundly established from Ibn ʿAbbās — Ibn ʿUyayna related it from ʿAmr ibn Dīnār from Ibn ʿAbbās — and soundly established from Ibn al-Zubayr, and related from ʿUmar and Ibn Masʿūd; these are four of the Companions. In addition it is the reading of Ibn Waththāb, al-Aʿmash, Ḥamza and al-Kisāʾī, and it is more in keeping with the verse-endings before and after it. The reading نَخِرَةً is that of the people of the two Sanctuaries, al-Ḥasan and Abū ʿAmr. Both readings are good, because the majority transmitted them.

nahhas-irab:12-12.t: It was said: the meaning is a return and a coming back, and they made it a losing one because they had been promised the Fire in it.

nahhas-irab:13-14.t: فَإِذا هُمْ بِالسَّاهِرَةِ (14): Sufyān said: الساهرة is a land in Syria. Saʿīd related from Qatāda: الساهرة is Hell. Abū Jaʿfar said: الساهرة in the speech of the Arabs is the wide, fearsome land in which one stays awake out of fear. Abū Ḥātim claimed that the implied form is "then behold, they are at الساهرة — by النازعات". This is a clear mistake, because one does not begin with the fāʾ, and النازعات is at the start of the surah. This is the fourth view on the answer to the oath.

nahhas-irab:15-15.t: هَلْ may be in the sense of «قد»; the lexicographers have reported that. It may also have its usual meaning.

nahhas-irab:16-16.t:
طُوىً with nunation (tanwīn) and ḍamma on the ṭāʾ is the reading of Ibn ʿĀmir and al-Kisāʾī. The reading of the people of Medina and Abū ʿAmr is without nunation and with ḍamma on the ṭāʾ. The reading of al-Ḥasan is طِوىً with kasra on the ṭāʾ and nunation; its meaning in his view is "in the valley that was hallowed twice and in which [Moses] was called". The reading with ḍamma on the ṭāʾ and nunation is on the basis that it is a name of the valley and not a deflected form (maʿdūl); it is just like your saying حطم, therefore it is declined as a triptote. Whoever does not decline it makes it deflected, like عمر. But al-Farrāʾ rejects that, because he claimed that he does not know in the speech of the Arabs any noun from roots with yāʾ or wāw that is deflected from فاعل to فُعَل. Abū Jaʿfar said: It is possible that the non-declension is on the basis that it is a name of the spot (البقعة), so it would be other than what he interpreted. It has been read without nunation by those whose word constitutes proof.
اذْهَبْ إِلى فِرْعَوْنَ إِنَّهُ طَغى (17): whoever says يطغى in the imperfect says طغيت, and it is الطغيان; whoever says يطغو says طغوت.

nahhas-irab:18-18.t: The reading of the people of Medina and the reading of Abū ʿAmr is تَزَّكَّى [with doubled zāy], and [the others read] تَزَكَّى with the zāy undoubled; the meaning and the implied form in Arabic are one, because the original of تزكى is تتزكى, and one tāʾ was omitted. Whoever says تزّكّى assimilated it (idghām). No difference between them is known. [Translator's note: the source says «قراءة أهل المدينة وقراءة أبي عمرو تَزَكَّى بتخفيف الزاي», which appears to have lost a word; Nāfiʿ and Ibn Kathīr are known to read with the doubled zāy. The bracketed additions follow the logic of the explanation.] Ibn Zayd said: «تزكّى» means "to submit (become Muslim)"; he said: every تزكية in the Qur'an is Islam.

nahhas-irab:19-19.t: وَأَهْدِيَكَ إِلى رَبِّكَ is conjoined, and likewise فَتَخْشى, i.e. so that you fear His punishment by abandoning disobedience to Him.

nahhas-irab:2-2.t: وَالنَّاشِطاتِ is conjoined (maʿṭūf) to النازعات, i.e. those who pull out the spirits swiftly; one says نشطه when he pulled it swiftly. However, al-Farrāʾ reported نشطه in the sense of "he tied it", and أنشطه "he untied it", and it is reported from the Arabs: كأنما أنشط من عقال ("as though he were released from a hobble"). He was contradicted in this, and the one who contradicted him cited as evidence the poet's saying: [al-rajaz] 536- أضحت همومي تنشط المناشطا (My cares have come to pull me in every direction.)

nahhas-irab:20-20.t: [الْآيَةَ الْكُبْرى] is among the [expressions] from which the alif and lām may not be omitted, nor may it be brought in the indefinite. [Translator's note: the source does not name the word discussed; الكبرى, an elative (afʿal) feminine form, is presumably meant.]

nahhas-irab:21-21.t: The meaning of the fāʾ is that it indicates that the second comes after the first, while the wāw is for combination. This is their basic meaning.

nahhas-irab:22-22.t: In the position of a ḥāl (circumstantial).

nahhas-irab:23-24.t: فَحَشَرَ: the object is omitted, i.e. "and he gathered his people", as Ibn Zayd said: he gathered his people, فَنادى among them فَقالَ أَنَا رَبُّكُمُ الْأَعْلى (24).

nahhas-irab:25-25.t: Al-Farrāʾ said: That is, Allah seized him with a seizing as an exemplary punishment (نكالا) for the last and the first.

nahhas-irab:26-26.t: That is, [for one who] fears Allah's punishment, as it befell someone else when he disobeyed.

nahhas-irab:27-27.t: أَأَنْتُمْ أَشَدُّ خَلْقاً أَمِ السَّماءُ: that is, why do you deny the resurrection when the creation of the heaven is harder than your resurrection?

nahhas-irab:28-28.t: That is, as a roof for the earth.

nahhas-irab:29-29.t: وَأَغْطَشَ لَيْلَها: a figurative annexation (iḍāfa majāz), because the meaning of night is the departure of the sun; since it sets in the sky, "its night" was said, as one says "the riding animal's saddle". Likewise وَأَخْرَجَ ضُحاها.

nahhas-irab:3-3.t: It is conjoined (maʿṭūf), i.e. "and by the angels who glide (السابحات)", meaning the swift ones. ʿAṭāʾ said: السَّابِحاتِ are the ships. سَبْحاً is a maṣdar (verbal noun).

nahhas-irab:30-30.t:
وَالْأَرْضَ is accusative by an implied verb, i.e. "and He spread out the earth". Al-Farrāʾ claimed ] [Translator's note: a stray bracket appears here in the source.] that the accusative and the nominative are both permissible, and that it is like وَالْقَمَرَ قَدَّرْناهُ مَنازِلَ [Yā Sīn: 39], meaning in [allowing] the nominative and the accusative.
Abū Jaʿfar said: There is a difference between them, because in His saying الْقَمَرَ قَدَّرْناهُ مَنازِلَ the nominative is good, since its implied form is "and a sign for them is the moon". In وَالْأَرْضَ بَعْدَ ذلِكَ دَحاها (30) the nominative is remote, because before it is something a verb has governed, and it is not connected to anything in the nominative. This is a clear difference. We know of no one who read «والأرض» in the nominative, whereas «والقمر» in the nominative was read by the leading readers.
There is a difficulty in the verse, because He, the Exalted, said: قُلْ أَإِنَّكُمْ لَتَكْفُرُونَ بِالَّذِي خَلَقَ الْأَرْضَ فِي يَوْمَيْنِ [Fuṣṣilat: 9], and after it ثُمَّ اسْتَوى إِلَى السَّماءِ, which indicates that the creation of the heaven came after the creation of the earth, while here [He says] وَالْأَرْضَ بَعْدَ ذلِكَ دَحاها (30). Among the soundest and best things said about this is what Ibn Abī Ṭalḥa related from Ibn ʿAbbās, who said: Allah, Majestic and Mighty is He, created the earth before the heaven and measured out its provisions in it, but did not spread it out; then He created the heaven, then spread out the earth after it. Mujāhid and al-Suddī said: وَالْأَرْضَ بَعْدَ ذلِكَ دَحاها means "together with that He spread it out", as He, Majestic and Mighty is He, said: عُتُلٍّ بَعْدَ ذلِكَ زَنِيمٍ [al-Qalam: 13]. Abū Jaʿfar said: The first view is preferable, so that the word keeps its usual meaning. The meaning of الدّحو in the language is spreading out; one says دحوت أدحو and دحيت أدحي, and from the second [form] the name دحية was given.

nahhas-irab:32-32.t: [وَالْجِبالَ is accusative] by an implied verb as well.

nahhas-irab:33-33.t: Al-Farrāʾ said: That is, He created that as a benefit and enjoyment for you. He said: The nominative is also permissible, like مَتاعٌ قَلِيلٌ [Āl ʿImrān: 197].

nahhas-irab:34-34.t: Ibn Abī Ṭalḥa related from Ibn ʿAbbās, who said: [الطَّامَّةُ is] the Resurrection; Allah magnified its matter and warned of it. Abū Jaʿfar said: When the Arabs magnify something, they describe it as الطامة (the overwhelming).

nahhas-irab:35-35.t: That is, when he reads his record and sees his place, he remembers his deeds.

nahhas-irab:36-36.t: He made الجحيم feminine because of the meaning "the Fire"; it is an epithet (naʿt) of it here.

nahhas-irab:37-39.t: مَنْ is in the position of the nominative as a mubtadaʾ (subject), and its khabar (predicate) is فَإِنَّ الْجَحِيمَ هِيَ الْمَأْوى (39). The implied form according to the Kufans is "then it is his abode (مأواه)", the alif [and lām] being a substitute for the pronoun; the implied form according to the Basrans is "it is the abode for him".

nahhas-irab:4-4.t: فَالسَّابِقاتِ سَبْقاً (4) فَالسَّابِقاتِ is conjoined (maʿṭūf), i.e. "and by the angels who outstrip the devils with the revelation". ʿAṭāʾ said: السابقات are the horses. سَبْقاً is a maṣdar (verbal noun).

nahhas-irab:40-40.t: وَأَمَّا مَنْ خافَ مَقامَ رَبِّهِ: i.e. the standing of the reckoning for his sins. وَنَهَى النَّفْسَ عَنِ الْهَوى: [الهوى] is inclination towards what is not good.

nahhas-irab:42-42.t: Al-Farrāʾ said: It may be said: anchoring (الإرساء) belongs only to the ship, the mountains and the like, so how is the Hour described with anchoring? The answer is that it is like the ship when it sails and then comes to anchor; its anchoring is its standing (قيامها), and that is not like the standing of one who stands on his feet and the like, but as you say: قام العدل ("justice was established"), قام الحقّ ("the truth was established"), i.e. it appeared and became firm.

nahhas-irab:43-43.t: That is, mentioning it is not your concern, because you do not know its time. The original is «في ما»; the alif was omitted to distinguish between the interrogative and the informative, since before ما there is a particle that puts it in the genitive. Pausing on it is فيمه, nothing else being permissible, so that the alif and the vowel of the mīm are not both lost. The correct thing is not to pause on it, so as not to differ from the written text (السواد) by adding the hāʾ, or to commit a solecism if one pauses on it without the hāʾ.

nahhas-irab:44-44.t: In the position of the nominative as a mubtadaʾ (subject), i.e. the ultimate knowledge of it.

nahhas-irab:45-45.t: Abū Jaʿfar, Ibn Muḥayṣin and Ṭalḥa read مُنْذِرٌ مَنْ يَخْشاها with nunation (tanwīn); this is the original, and it is only omitted for lightness. [Translator's note: the source prints the phrase as «مُنْذِرُ مَنْ يَخْشاها» without the tanwīn sign, although it describes the nunated reading.]

nahhas-irab:46-46.t: That is, what they were in has passed away from them, so they do not think about what has gone and it seems little to them. In this there is a sense of warning to whoever is deluded by this world and his safety in it, that he will leave it shortly, and the pleasure and joy he found in it will leave him, as though he had remained in it only an evening or its morning.

nahhas-irab:5-5.t:
فَالْمُدَبِّراتِ is conjoined, i.e. "and by the angels". He said: There is no disagreement among the people of knowledge about this, that the angels are meant by it, and it is figurative (majāz), because Allah, Majestic and Mighty is He, is the One who arranges (al-mudabbir) all things. He said: يُدَبِّرُ الْأَمْرَ مِنَ السَّماءِ إِلَى الْأَرْضِ [al-Sajda: 5]. Since the angels, Allah's blessings be upon them, descend with the revelation, the rulings and the dispensing of the rains, they were called مدبرات figuratively. Al-Farrāʾ said: It is as He said: فَإِنَّهُ نَزَّلَهُ عَلى قَلْبِكَ [al-Baqara: 97], ascribing the sending down to Jibrāʾīl, peace be upon him, while it is Allah who sent it down; and likewise نَزَلَ بِهِ الرُّوحُ الْأَمِينُ [al-Shuʿarāʾ: 193]. أَمْراً is accusative as a maṣdar (verbal noun). It is also possible that the implied form is "those who arrange by a command from Allah", the bāʾ being omitted so that the verb passes on directly; Sībawayh recited: [al-basīṭ] 537-
أمرتك الخير فافعل ما أمرت به ... فقد تركتك ذا مال وذا نشب
(I commanded you to do good, so do what you were commanded, for I have left you possessed of wealth and property.)
As for the answer to the oath (jawāb al-qasam), there are four views about it. The soundest and best of them is that it is omitted, something clearly indicating it; the meaning is "by النازعات, you will surely be resurrected", and they said: "Shall we be resurrected when we are decayed bones?" Their saying أَإِذا كُنَّا indicates that omitted [answer]. It was said [secondly]: the answer is إِنَّ فِي ذلِكَ لَعِبْرَةً لِمَنْ يَخْشى (26); this is far-fetched, because what lies between them is very distant. It was said [thirdly]: only the lām was omitted, the implied form being "on the day the quaking quakes" (ليوم ترجف الراجفة). This too is even more far-fetched than that, because the lām is not among the things that are omitted, since it occurs on most things, so one would not know where it was omitted from; and if its omission were permissible, والله زيد منطلق would be permissible in the sense [of having] the lām. Ibn Abī Ṭalḥa related from Ibn ʿAbbās: الرَّاجِفَةُ is the first blast, and الرَّادِفَةُ is the second. Abū Hurayra related from the Prophet ﷺ: between them are forty.

nahhas-irab:8-8.t: A mubtadaʾ (subject) and khabar (predicate). ʿAṭāʾ said: واجفة means moving; someone else said: fearful.

nahhas-irab:9-9.t: A mubtadaʾ (subject) and its khabar (predicate); [the meaning is] that they are abased because of their disgrace on the Day of Resurrection for their sins. The statement is complete here.
